hook.line: No spoken line; a song plays while someone types 'hello' to ChatGPT.
hook.visual: Dark phone screen recording of the ChatGPT app: keyboard up, 'hello' typed and sent, small 'chatgpt?!?!' caption mid-frame.

beats.what: Empty ChatGPT chat, keyboard open, 'chatgpt?!?!' caption in the middle
ChatGPT answers in slang: 'Yooo what's good?'
A long reply about recovery validation appears
'zip compression test' sent; the bot calls the user 'chief'
Bot writes a Python ZIP recovery script
Closing message: archive created and verified

why_it_works: The bot's odd casual persona ('chief', 'Yooo') breaks the expectation of a normal assistant, so the viewer keeps watching to see what it does next
Only 14 s with no cuts and a high loop score, so the screen replays before the viewer decides to scroll
The 'chatgpt?!?!' caption frames everything as a surprise without explaining it, which pulls comments
weaknesses: Nothing is explained; the viewer cannot tell what was prompted or why it matters
Text is tiny (median text height under 2% of the frame) and most of it sits outside the safe area
No face and no voice, so there is no creator to follow
for_robert: Avoid the silent mystery screen recording; borrow only the reaction caption idea: have Fred react with a short '?!?!' bubble when a chatbot answer looks strange, then Robert explains it.
